opening.argument: The calls are presented as recorded examples intended to show viewers what fraudulent callers might say, not as an offer for viewers to pursue. The narrator expressly identifies the interaction as “an example of a fake scam call” and warns that “Apple is not going to call you and get you to go to those sites.” The surrounding guidance reinforces that purpose: viewers are told, “If you get a call, just hang up,” and are warned to stay away from those scams. Although the caller directs the listener toward an external website and mentions a security scan, the listener reports difficulty reaching it and says the callers hung up; the evidence does not establish that the connection was completed, credentials were provided, or any loss occurred.

citations.quote: I have been receiving multiple calls from scammers and several today so I recorded a few in case you speak to someone so you know what they might tell you.

Apple is not going to call you and get you to go to those sites.
If you get a call, just hang up.
